sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: Students in Grades 3 and 4 have explored soil, air and water.
sections.source_evidence: Students in Grades 3 and 4 have explored soil, air and water.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: They also learned how life evolves in different landforms depending upon the availability of soil, air, water and sunlight.
sections.source_evidence: They also learned how life evolves in different landforms depending upon the availability of soil, air, water and sunlight.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: This unit in Grade 5 presents the importance of water in life and ecosystems.
sections.source_evidence: This unit in Grade 5 presents the importance of water in life and ecosystems.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: It also covers its various forms, movement, and role in shaping land and supporting habitats.
sections.source_evidence: It also covers its various forms, movement, and role in shaping land and supporting habitats.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: The unit conveys water as a unique and limited essence of life — showing how it helps in sustaining the life on Earth.
sections.source_evidence: The unit conveys water as a unique and limited essence of life — showing how it helps in sustaining the life on Earth.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: It also gives examples from the lives of people, who stay close to nature.
sections.source_evidence: It also gives examples from the lives of people, who stay close to nature.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: They enjoy clean treasures from nature and develop various materials available from nearby forest and surroundings.
sections.source_evidence: They enjoy clean treasures from nature and develop various materials available from nearby forest and surroundings.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Their lifestyles and productions with locally available materials reflect how life can be happy, and creative in the lap of nature.
sections.source_evidence: Their lifestyles and productions with locally available materials reflect how life can be happy, and creative in the lap of nature.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: How to Facilitate • Encourage students to think about water bodies near their homes or schools.
sections.source_evidence: How to Facilitate • Encourage students to think about water bodies near their homes or schools.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Inspire them to explore where the water comes from and where it goes. • The Activity 6 in Chapter 1 on mustard seed shows how rivers flow from higher to lower ground and follow the shape of the land.
sections.source_evidence: Inspire them to explore where the water comes from and where it goes. • The Activity 6 in Chapter 1 on mustard seed shows how rivers flow from higher to lower ground and follow the shape of the land.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Use the map of India to explore which rivers flow into which seas and how landforms (like mountains) guide their direction. • Talk about what happens to rainwater in their school or neighbourhood.
sections.source_evidence: Use the map of India to explore which rivers flow into which seas and how landforms (like mountains) guide their direction. • Talk about what happens to rainwater in their school or neighbourhood.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: Use this to start a conversation on how cities and villages plan for water. • Help students list different ways in which water plays an important role in our life.
sections.source_evidence: Use this to start a conversation on how cities and villages plan for water. • Help students list different ways in which water plays an important role in our life.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Connect this to ideas of sharing and saving water.
sections.source_evidence: Connect this to ideas of sharing and saving water.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Let them think about how water is stored in their homes (tanks, pots, etc.) and how a dam works as a big water storing unit. • Engage students in role-plays to critically think about both the scarcity and excess of water. • Encourage students to discuss with their parents or grandparents about festivals, stories, or memories connected to rivers.
sections.source_evidence: Let them think about how water is stored in their homes (tanks, pots, etc.) and how a dam works as a big water storing unit. • Engage students in role-plays to critically think about both the scarcity and excess of water. • Encourage students to discuss with their parents or grandparents about festivals, stories, or memories connected to rivers.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: This will help them see rivers not just as physical things, but as part of their community and culture.
sections.source_evidence: This will help them see rivers not just as physical things, but as part of their community and culture.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Note to the Teacher This unit includes two chapters: Chapter 1 ‘Water — The Essence of Life’ and Chapter 2 ‘Journey of a River’.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: It also highlights the importance of water in different activities in the society.

sections.content: This chapter introduces the continuous movement of water in different forms through the water cycle.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: It also explores how water shapes the land and supports life in freshwater habitats, and highlights the need to conserve water.
